target_customer: Hospitals and clinicians performing vascular access, especially central line placement, and ultrasound training programs
problem: 2D ultrasound forces clinicians to imagine 3D anatomy while moving the probe; about half of beginners fail on a first central line attempt and existing 3D devices cost over ten times as much.
business_model: Medical device sales (3D ultrasound system with AI and mixed reality guidance)

founders.name: Tri Vu
founders.background_notes: Trained in Junjie Yao's Photoacoustic Imaging Lab at Duke (Duke PAI Lab page).

founders.name: Luca Menozzi
education: Duke, PhD in ultrasound and photoacoustic imaging
founders.background_notes: A Duke page lists a January 2025 Nature Communications paper on the underlying method.

competitors.name: Fujifilm Sonosite iLOOK
competitors.traction_then: Sonosite is the long-time leader in vascular access ultrasound

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time volumetric ultrasound at low cost needs novel transducer and reconstruction work, plus FDA clearance; the founders come from a lab that published the method.

defensibility.rationale: Duke patent estate and a provisional patent on the mixed reality interface are reported by a directory (unverified); FDA clearance would add a moat but has not happened.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move against this wedge found as of late 2026.

market_need_then: Central line placement has a high first attempt failure rate among beginners per the company; hospitals spend heavily on ultrasound training. Demand evidence is company stated.

branding.domain_note: Uses lumius-imaging.com, not an exact lumius.com match.

identity.logo: not described by any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Short declarative lines such as Make ultrasound ubiquitous and We believe

branding.brand_signature: The 3D camera for the body tagline

brand_strength.rationale: Little public brand footprint beyond YC launch and Duke coverage.

outcome_analysis: Lumius is an active Spring 2026 company with no exit. It is a Duke spinout selected by Y Combinator in March 2026 and still raising a seed round as of June 2026 according to a report found in search; the product is not FDA cleared, so the main risks are regulatory timing, hardware cost targets and incumbent response.
notes: No round amounts found. A directory lists the stage as pre-seed with no amount; the website lists Boost VC, FundersClub and Robinhood Ventures as supporters without stating roles, so they are not recorded as round investors. Duke names Chenhang Li as a third founder, but the YC page lists two founders, so only two are recorded. Competitor Fujifilm iLOOK is dated July 2026, after the March batch start, so it is a near batch reference only. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition.
